7 اندال القَوْمُ The people, or party, removed, or shifted, from one place to another. (S.) ―
-b2- اندال مَا فِىبَطْنِهِ What was in his belly, (M, K,) of intestines or peritonæum, (M,) came forth, (M, K,) in consequence of its being pierced. (M.) ―
-b3- And اندال It (the belly) became wide, and near, or approaching, to the ground. (M, K.) Also (K) It (the belly) was, or became, flaccid, flabby, or pendulous; (S, O, K;) and so ↓ دَالَ . (K.) ―
-b4- And It (a thing) dangled, or moved to and fro; and hung. (M, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
